The property of seeming true, of resembling reality; resemblance to reality.
A statement which merely appears to be true.
Faithfulness to its own rules; internal cohesion.

examples.text: On July 12, Madame filed suit for divorce, naming one Jane McManus as his principal mistress. Other adulteries were noted in the interest of verisimilitude.

glosses: The probability of a specified outcome; the chance of something happening; probability; the state or degree of being probable.

examples.text: In all likelihood the meeting will be cancelled.
The likelihood is that the inflation rate will continue to rise.
While starting early can increase your likelihood of attaining millionaire status, the investments you choose play an equally important role.

glosses: The probability that some fixed outcome was generated by a random distribution with a specific parameter.
Likeness, resemblance.

examples.text: There is no likelihood between pure light and black darkness, […]or between righteousness and reprobation.

glosses: Appearance, show, sign, expression.
The quality of deserving applause, praiseworthiness; something worthy of praise.

examples.text: integrity, fidelity, and other gracious plausibilities

glosses: The appearance of truth, especially when deceptive; speciousness.

examples.text: Plausibility, I know, can only be unmasked by shewing the absurdities it glosses over, and the simple truths it involves with specious errors.

glosses: A plausible statement, argument etc.

examples.text: She too must shimmer through the gloom o' the grave, / Come and confront me— […] / Striking me dumb, and helping her to speak, / Tell her own story her own way, and turn / My plausibility to nothingness!

glosses: The fact of being believable; believability, credibility.
